question.question:
Use exact arithmetic. A firm's unlevered value is 710 USD million. Base EBIT is 55 USD million and management reports a one-time EBIT revision of 5 USD million, where a positive figure raises EBIT and a negative figure is a loss that lowers it; adjusted EBIT is base EBIT plus the signed revision. The corporate tax rate is 24 percent. The firm must pick one debt level from the grid 0, 1, 2, 3 or 4 times 70 USD million. Debt at grid level k (k from 1 to 4) carries an annual interest rate of 6 percent plus 1 percentage point for each level above level 1, so level 1 pays 6 percent. A level is admissible only if its annual interest, debt times its rate, does not exceed adjusted EBIT; level 0 is always admissible. For each admissible level, firm value equals unlevered value plus a tax shield of tax rate times debt, minus an expected distress cost of 35 percent of the debt above a threshold equal to 4 times adjusted EBIT (zero if debt is at or below the threshold). The firm chooses the admissible level with the highest firm value; ties go to the lower debt level. Equity value is the chosen firm value minus the chosen debt. Report the equity value in USD million.

Answer format: return only the exact numeric value interpreted in `usd_million`, using finite-decimal notation when it terminates in base 10 and an irreducible `numerator/denominator` fraction otherwise, with no unit label or additional text.
